transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we dive into the design review, I want to make sure we're all on the same page about the courtyard set for Soundstage 3. We're weighing two options: a masonry courtyard or a modular painted-timber courtyard. The approved construction budget is $180,000, and fabrication can't begin until we've completed this review and I've signed off on the final plan. I'd like to hear from each of you — structural, permits, stunt, and insurance — so we can make an informed decision today. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical structural issue before we go further. My load test yesterday found that the masonry courtyard design would exceed Soundstage 3's 600 kilograms-per-square-meter floor limit. The modular painted-timber design does pass, but only if we install a 30-millimeter load-spreading deck. My written report is still in the engineering queue, so I want to make sure everyone hears this directly from me now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share what I confirmed with the local heritage-permit office this morning. The approved facade may be no wider than exactly 8 meters, and on-stage masonry cutting is prohibited. The permit clerk's email hasn't been added to the production file yet, so I want everyone to hear this directly from me now — especially given that Jonah's structural findings and these permit constraints both bear directly on whether the masonry option is even viable.
